kurz: How the costs of an ETF can be measured by its gap to the index, and why this gap is often smaller than the total expense ratio in the prospectus.

bloecke.md:
The total expense ratio (TER) is the easiest ETF figure to find, and its informative value is easily overestimated. It states what share of the fund assets the provider took in the past financial year for management, custody, audit and the index licence. It does not show how much the investor has lost relative to the index.

It does not include the fund's transaction costs for index changes, the swap fee for synthetic replication or the withholding tax deducted from dividends at fund level. Also missing, with the opposite sign, is the income from [[Securities lending|securities lending]]. Together, these items are often larger than the fee itself, and they do not all work in the same direction. The TER therefore gives the published price. What the fund has cost the investor is shown only by the measured gap to the index.

bloecke.formel: Tracking difference = Index return − Fund return   (percentage points, same period, same currency)
bloecke.erklaerung: The realised shortfall of an index fund relative to its index. Because it is derived after the fact from two returns, it contains every type of cost, every tax effect and every item of additional income, even if these are not known individually.
variablen: Return of the tracked index, usually as a net index, that is, after an assumed deduction of withholding tax
Performance of the unit including reinvested distributions
positive = the fund lags behind; negative = the fund is ahead of the index
bloecke.beispiel: Index +12.40%, fund +12.25% in the same calendar year: tracking difference 0.15 percentage points. With a TER of 0.20%, the fund has thus recouped 0.05 percentage points of its own fee.

bloecke.md: Some data providers calculate the other way round, that is, fund return minus index return, and thereby reverse the sign. Before evaluating a table of tracking differences, it must therefore be clear which sign indicates a shortfall. The simplest way is to compare the values with the TER. If the typical amount is of the same order of magnitude as the fee and has no minus sign, the table measures the shortfall.

bloecke.md:
## Reasons for a shortfall below the fee

Four sources explain the difference. None of them is based on the skill of the fund management.

- In securities lending, the fund lends shares in return for a fee. The collateral is valued daily and typically amounts to 102% to 105% of the value lent. At iShares, 62.5% of lending income goes to the fund assets and the provider keeps 37.5%.
- The index methodology also plays a role. Many ETFs measure themselves against a net index that assumes a flat-rate deduction of withholding tax. If the fund pays less withholding tax thanks to its domicile, it collects more in dividends than the index assumes.
- The swap structure has an effect in synthetic replication of certain qualified US indices, because under US law no withholding tax is due there on the dividend component. According to a justETF analysis, the measured lead of synthetic S&P 500 ETFs over physical ones is of the order of 0.12 to 0.26 percentage points a year.
- With sampling, the fund does not buy all the stocks. It thereby saves transaction costs and accepts a small deviation that can go either way.

Lending income depends on demand for the securities lent, and tax structures depend on legal situations that change. A tracking difference that turns out negative in a single year allows no conclusion about the next year. The figure only becomes reliable as an average over three to five calendar years, and even then it remains a measurement of the past.

## Fund domicile and ISIN

Ireland has a double taxation agreement with the US (signed on 28 July 1997) under which funds domiciled in Ireland usually bear 15% instead of 30% [[Withholding tax|withholding tax]] on US dividends. Luxembourg physical funds pay the full rate in practice. The domicile can be read from the first two characters of the ISIN, IE or LU.

With an assumed US dividend yield of 1.6%, this corresponds to about 0.24 versus 0.48 percentage points of return a year. For the MSCI World, whose US share was 72.14% on 31 August 2026, the same assumptions give a leakage from US dividends of around 0.17 percentage points for an Irish fund (72% of 0.24). These amounts do not appear on any tax certificate. They arise at fund level and reduce the [[Net asset value (NAV)|net asset value]]. Since the 2018 investment tax reform, private investors can no longer credit them against their own tax. Since then, the fund itself has paid tax on certain domestic income (Section 6 in conjunction with Section 7 InvStG, Investment Tax Act), and in return the investor receives the flat-rate [[Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)|partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)]] under Section 20 InvStG. According to the explanatory memorandum to the law, the partial exemption is also intended to compensate, on a flat-rate basis, for withholding tax on foreign dividends insofar as double taxation agreements do not refund it. Because the rate is the same for all equity funds, a fund with higher withholding tax nevertheless remains at a disadvantage.

bloecke.md:
For the partial exemption, what counts is the binding ratio commitment in the investment conditions (Anlagebedingungen) rather than the portfolio the fund holds. For an equity fund, the investment conditions must commit to more than 50% equity participations (Section 2(6) InvStG). Individual swap and specialised products do not commit to this and therefore receive 0% instead of 30% partial exemption, even though they in fact track an equity index.

With a realised price gain of €50,000 and 26.375% [[Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)|flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer)]], the tax is then €13,188 instead of €9,231, that is, €3,956 more. A withholding tax advantage of 0.2 percentage points a year brings around €300 a year on a portfolio of €150,000. Calculated with these fixed amounts, the tax disadvantage would be offset after around 13 years. The disadvantage grows too, however, because the price gain that is taxed without the partial exemption grows along with the portfolio, and because the extra return of the swap fund is also taxed in full. Calculating with a lump-sum investment, an annual return of 5% to 7% and tax on sale, the swap fund comes out ahead after tax only after around 50 years. The advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale), which is taxed more heavily every year without partial exemption, pushes this point even further out.

## The spread as a one-off cost

Market makers base their binding bid and ask prices on the indicative net asset value, which is recalculated every 15 to 60 seconds during trading hours. For the two most actively traded world ETFs, the Xetra Liquidity Measure (XLM), which states what an immediate purchase and sale of €100,000 costs as a result of the spread and market depth, stood at around 2 basis points in September 2026. The figure varies considerably depending on the day and the time of day. Continuous trading runs from 9:00 to 17:30. From 15:30 the US stock exchanges are open, and the US shares in the fund are valued at current prices instead of being estimated. The spread is widest at the start and end of the trading day. Without a limit order, you are exposed to this risk without protection.

The spread and the TER differ above all in how often they are incurred. The [[Spread|spread]] is a percentage of the amount traded and is incurred once; the TER is a percentage of the holding and is incurred every year. How much the spread matters therefore depends less on its size than on the holding period.

bloecke.titel: Worked examples on spread and TER
bloecke.md:
With a lump-sum investment of €20,000 and a quoted spread of 0.04%, half the spread, 0.02%, costs €4. The TER of 0.20% costs €40 in the first year. The trading mark-up therefore corresponds to just over five weeks of ongoing costs and is incurred only once.

With a savings plan of €300 a month, €3,600 is traded in a year, and 0.02% of that is 72 cents. As soon as the portfolio is worth more than about €360, the ongoing fee is the larger item.

When an existing holding is switched into an ETF that is 0.03 percentage points cheaper, the full spread is incurred on the sale and on the purchase, plus order fees. If there are gains, tax also becomes due immediately, and this amount would otherwise have stayed invested. Such a switch is almost never worthwhile.

schritte.titel: Record the index and index variant
schritte.text: In addition to the index name, such as “MSCI World”, the variant is also recorded, that is, net, gross or price return index. Confusing the net and gross index produces a deviation of the order of the entire withholding tax; a comparison with the price return index produces a deviation equal to the entire dividend yield.

The comparison is made in the same currency and the same share class, and distributions are reinvested in the calculation. A distributing and an accumulating unit of the same fund are not comparable without this adjustment.

schritte.titel: Set several calendar years side by side
schritte.text: Sources are the provider's annual reports or comparison portals. Three to five years are examined, each year individually, because an average alone does not show whether it is driven by a single outlier year.
Compare a value with the known TER and deduce from it which sign indicates a shortfall.

The difference between the average tracking differences of the two funds multiplied by the portfolio value gives the amount in euros per year. For an existing holding, a switch for less than a few hundredths of a percentage point is practically never worthwhile, because the spread and tax are incurred immediately.

bloecke.md: The table shows only the cost effect and assumes the same gross return for all rows. Real products also differ in their index, and an S&P 500 ETF is no substitute for a world ETF. The rows therefore stand for cost levels and do not form a product ranking. This is why the statement is robust: the cost difference has the same effect in every scenario, whereas the difference in returns between the indices is unknown. Lower costs are a certain saving; a higher return from a different index remains uncertain.

bloecke.md: The TER states the published price; the tracking difference shows what the fund actually cost. When comparing two ETFs on the same index, first set the average tracking differences over several years side by side. Only then look at the fee, in order to understand where the difference comes from.

mitnehmen: The TER explains only part of the gap to the index, because transaction costs, withholding tax and lending income are not included in it.
The tracking difference measures the realised shortfall relative to the index and should be averaged over three to five years, not taken from a single year.
A shortfall below the TER is normal and no proof of special skill on the part of the provider; this advantage can disappear if lending demand or tax rules change.
Two ETFs on the same index differ by something of the order of 0.2 percentage points a year through their domicile alone (IE instead of LU ISIN).
The spread is incurred once on the volume traded and the TER every year on the holding, which is why switching is more expensive than it seems at first glance.

begriffe.text: Difference between index return and fund return over the same period, in percentage points. Unlike the TER, it includes all types of cost, including transaction costs, withholding tax and lending income. In the more common convention, negative values mean that the fund is ahead of the index.

Standard deviation of the ongoing deviations between fund and index. It measures how evenly the index is tracked and says nothing about the costs of doing so. Even a permanently expensive fund can have a very small tracking error.

Share of the fund assets that the provider took in the financial year for management, custody, audit and the index licence. The fund's transaction costs, swap fees and taxes at fund level are not included.

Portion of dividends that is withheld in the company's country of domicile and does not reach the fund. It reduces the net asset value, and since the 2018 investment tax reform, private investors can no longer credit it against their own tax.
Estimated value of the fund assets per unit, calculated every 15 to 60 seconds during trading hours. Market makers base their binding bid and ask prices on it.
